headline: Migration phenotypes and decisions emerging from interaction structure in minimal models
label: Emergent Cell Behaviour Models
summary: Recent preprint and published work treats leader-follower phenotypes and branching-polarity decisions as emergent outputs of cell interactions rather than…
synthesis: The dominant thread is treating discrete cell phenotypes and migration decisions as emergent outputs of interaction structure rather than prescribed rules. A polarity-based agent-based model of cranial neural crest cell migration produces leader and follower phenotypes spontaneously from collective dynamics. A coarse-grained hexagonal-network model, paired with live-cell imaging of macrophage and endothelial migration, frames decision-making as a trade-off between protrusion branching and polarity. A landmark-free shape-space tool provides a quantitative means to map morphological transitions in migrating cells. The items do not share a common mechanism or scale. What is new is the explicit linkage of phenotype and decision-making to the topology of cell interactions.
